newsitem.title: CHINA: China to close Mao Zedong mausoleum for renovation.
newsitem.headline: China to close Mao Zedong mausoleum for renovation.

text.p: China is to close for renovation the mausoleum in the heart of Beijing where the embalmed body of Chairman Mao Zedong has lain for 20 years, officials said on Friday.
The mausoleum will be closed to visitors from April 1 to December 31, an official of the mausoleum administrative office said.
"We need to do some renovation work on the interior, after all the hall has been open for 20 years," the official said.

However, he declined to say whether any of the renovation work would include touching up the embalmed body of Mao, who died on September 9, 1976. "I can't tell you specifics of what we will do," the official said.
More than 110 million people have filed past the body of Mao, which lies in a crystal sarcophagus, surrounded by flowers and military guards, since the mausoleum opened on September 9, 1977.
Visitors in 1996 numbered between seven and eight million.

The late paramount leader Deng Xiaoping, who died last month, abhorred the cult of personality that surrounded Mao and had his ashes scattered at sea and ordered that no memorial be set up to his memory.
